description: New Jersey-only rules checked against the cited MVC and Division of Highway Traffic Safety pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, New Jersey's speed limit in school zones, business districts, or residential districts is
questions.explanation: The official New Jersey driving FAQ says the speed limit, unless otherwise posted, is 25 mph in school zones, business, or residential districts. It does not set a single number that overrides a posted limit.

provenance.manual: State of New Jersey driving FAQ

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, New Jersey sets 35 mph
questions.explanation: The official New Jersey driving FAQ lists 35 mph in certain low density business and residential districts, separate from the 25 mph school, business, or residential figure.

provenance.manual: State of New Jersey driving FAQ

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, New Jersey's limit on all other roadways, after the 25 and 35 mph districts, is
questions.explanation: The official New Jersey driving FAQ says 50 mph on all other roadways, after listing the 25 mph and 35 mph districts.

provenance.manual: State of New Jersey driving FAQ

questions.q: New Jersey's FAQ describes interstate and 65 mph limits as
options: no numeric interstate limit at all
questions.explanation: The official New Jersey driving FAQ says 55 mph on certain state highways (as posted) and all interstates, and 65 mph on certain state highways (as posted). It does not make 65 the default interstate speed.

provenance.manual: State of New Jersey driving FAQ

questions.q: New Jersey's Division of Highway Traffic Safety states that drunk driving includes operating with a BAC of
options: 0.02 percent or greater for every driver
questions.explanation: The Division of Highway Traffic Safety brochure states that a person is guilty of drunk driving if he or she operates a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or greater. The same brochure says a driver can also be convicted of driving under the influence of intoxicating liquor when the BAC is below 0.08 percent.

provenance.manual: New Jersey Division of Highway Traffic Safety

questions.q: New Jersey's zero-tolerance description for a driver under 21 is
options: 0.08 BAC, the same as an adult
questions.explanation: The Division of Highway Traffic Safety brochure says that if you are under 21 and drive with any detectable amount of alcohol, described as .01 BAC or above, and are convicted of the zero-tolerance law, penalties apply. A commercial 0.04 rule was not on this page.

provenance.manual: New Jersey Division of Highway Traffic Safety

questions.q: Under the New Jersey highway-safety brochure, a BAC under 0.08
options: always proves the driver is not guilty
can still support a DUI conviction
is legal for a driver under 21
questions.explanation: The Division of Highway Traffic Safety brochure says that although the law refers to a 0.08 percent BAC, a person can be convicted of driving while under the influence of intoxicating liquor even when the BAC is below 0.08 percent.

provenance.manual: New Jersey Division of Highway Traffic Safety

questions.q: New Jersey's current remedial-driver page says the Probationary Driver Program is required when a probationary driver
questions.explanation: The Motor Vehicle Commission remedial-driver page says the Probationary Driver Program is a requirement for probationary driver's license holders who accumulate more than two motor vehicle points or are convicted of certain motor vehicle violations. The page does not state a 12-point suspension number.

questions.q: Successful completion of New Jersey's Driver Improvement Program
options: does not change the point total
questions.explanation: The Motor Vehicle Commission remedial-driver page describes the Driver Improvement Program as a non-probationary program that results in the removal of three points upon successful completion.

questions.q: A New Jersey driver whose license is subject to suspension or revocation may
options: ignore the suspension if points are under 20
take a 3-hour course in lieu of all or part of suspension
transfer the points to a passenger
wait 10 years for points to disappear automatically
questions.explanation: The Motor Vehicle Commission remedial-driver page says holders of a driver's license subject to suspension or revocation may elect to attend a three-hour Driver Improvement Program in lieu of all or part of a period of suspension. That page does not state a fixed point total that triggers the suspension.

questions.q: New Jersey's current remedial page ties the Driver Improvement Program to
options: a published 12-to-14-point rule that is stated on that page
removal of three points and a course option in lieu of suspension
a 4-point advisory that suspends a probationary driver for one year
no point reduction of any kind
questions.explanation: The page now posted at the remedial-driver address states the three-point removal and the election to attend a three-hour course in lieu of all or part of a suspension. It does not print a 12-to-14-point trigger. An older MVC address that once described 12 to 14 points now says the link has changed, so that number is not used here.

questions.q: A New Jersey permit holder must be supervised in the front seat by an adult who is
options: at least 18 with a valid license
any licensed parent, with no age stated
questions.explanation: The MVC first-license page requires an adult supervising driver in the front seat who is at least 21, has a valid New Jersey driver's license, and has a minimum of three years of driving experience.

questions.q: For a New Jersey permit issued to a driver under 21 on or after February 1, 2025, the practice requirement before a probationary license is
options: 6 months of driving with no hour total
questions.explanation: The MVC news release of January 31, 2025 says that starting February 1, 2025, under-21 holders of a special learner's permit or examination permit issued on or after that date must complete at least 50 hours of practice driving, 10 during darkness, and certify it on Form BA-CSD. The passenger rule on the first-license page separately allows parents, guardians, or dependents, and only one additional passenger unless a parent or guardian is along. A dependent means the driver's child, not a brother or sister.

questions.q: In New Jersey, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: New Jersey issues a learner's permit for a car at 16 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In New Jersey, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: New Jersey requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in New Jersey complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: New Jersey requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a New Jersey teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: New Jersey requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In New Jersey, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In New Jersey, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 17 years.

questions.q: In New Jersey, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: New Jersey drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the New Jersey car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The New Jersey car knowledge test has 50 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the New Jersey car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the New Jersey car knowledge test.

questions.q: In New Jersey, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In New Jersey, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

provenance.manual: NJ Division of Highway Traffic Safety DUI brochure

questions.q: In New Jersey, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: New Jersey sets the under-21 limit at 0.01%.

provenance.manual: NJ Division of Highway Traffic Safety DUI brochure

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in New Jersey?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in New Jersey can be posted up to 65 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes New Jersey's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
questions.explanation: New Jersey: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: How is New Jersey's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: New Jersey seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: State of New Jersey OAG press release

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in New Jersey?
questions.explanation: New Jersey requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is New Jersey's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: New Jersey requires at least $35,000 / $70,000 / $25,000.

provenance.manual: NJ DOBI Auto Insurance Buyers' Guide (2026)
